::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[solution to equations $x(1-y)=0$ and $y(1-x)=0$](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/4700486/solution-to-equations-x1-y-0-and-y1-x-0), asked by [Lenny White](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/696467/lenny-white) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2023-05-16; [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)):

> I need to solve two equations:
>
> $$x(1-y)=0 \\
> y(1-x)=0$$
>
> If I had one equation, ex $x(1-y)$, the solution would be $x=0$ or $y = 1$. But how do I go about solving two such equations? Are the solutions as below?
> $$x = 0 \lor y=0 \\
> x = 0 \lor y=1 \\
> x = 1 \lor y=0 \\
> x = 1 \lor y=1$$
:::

*Both* equations in the system need to be satisfied.

 - Equation 1 says: either $x=0$ or $y=1$
 - Equation 2 says: either $y=0$ or $x=1$

If you choose $x=0$ from equation 1, then you can't choose $x=1$ for equation 2. So $y=0$.

Likewise, if you choose $y=1$ from equation 1, then you can't choose $y=0$ for equation 2. So $x=1$.

If you want to do it with boolean algebra, you have:
$$\begin{aligned}
    ((x=0) \lor (y=1)) \land ((y=0) \lor (x=1))
    &= ((x=0) \land (y=0)) \lor ((x=0) \land (x=1)) \lor ((y=1) \land (y=0)) \lor ((y=1) \land (x=1))
  \\&= ((x=0) \land (y=0)) \lor \text{FALSE} \lor \text{FALSE} \lor ((y=1) \land (x=1))
  \\&= ((x=0) \land (y=0)) \lor ((y=1) \land (x=1))
\end{aligned}$$
